summary: Both sides draw the identical static 8-octant RGB test field (x→R, y→G, z→B, binary corners, zero motion over 600 s), but the port includes the exact-0.5 midplane in the HIGH half where the original excludes it, so on any lattice that samples coordinate 0.5 exactly — including the harness default 5x5x5 cloud — 48.8% of pixels take the wrong octant colour and mean brightness runs 153 vs 102.
observations: Both sides are completely STATIC, not animated: motion 0 and motionLit 0 on every captured frame in every run — baseline (120 frames @20fps), survey (300 @5fps), survey-600 (1200 frames over 600 s @2fps) all report zeroMotionFrames == capturedFrames on both sides, brightnessTrend 'steady', meanBrightness min==max==avg. Per-side --dump comparison confirms the frame at t=0 is byte-identical to t=3 s, t=5.5 s, t=300 s and t=319 s. There is no regime structure, no mode rotation, no warm-up transient: the survey revealed exactly one regime.

Both sides render exactly 8 distinct colours on the default 5x5x5 cloud, and they are the SAME 8: (0,0,0), (255,0,0), (0,255,0), (255,255,0), (0,0,255), (255,0,255), (0,255,255), (255,255,255) — pure binary RGB corners, no intermediate values, no gamma/dimming on either side.

Axis→channel assignment is IDENTICAL on both sides: fastest-varying pixel index (x) → red, middle index (y) → green, slowest index (z) → blue. No axis swap, no mirroring, no index-order difference. Verified on 3^3, 5^3, 7^3, 10^3, 11^3 and 21^3 lattices.

THE ONLY DIVERGENCE is the comparison at the exact midpoint. Original: a channel lights when its normalized coordinate is STRICTLY greater than 0.5 (coord == 0.5 → channel OFF). Port: channel lights when coord is >= 0.5 (coord == 0.5 → channel ON). Threshold bracketing from the 21^3 lattice (0.05 coordinate step): orig's first lit index sits at coord 0.55 with 0.50 still dark, so orig threshold ∈ (0.50, 0.55]; port's first lit index sits at coord 0.50 with 0.45 dark, so port threshold ∈ (0.45, 0.50]. Both are 'the 0.5 plane', differing only in strictness.

On EVEN-sided lattices the two sides are byte-identical. --pixels 1000 (10x10x10, coords 0, 1/9, … 1 — never exactly 0.5) produced identical frames on both sides: mean 128 vs 128, and a full frame-array comparison returned true. So the port is not 'a different pattern' — it agrees perfectly wherever no pixel lands on the midplane.

On ODD-sided lattices (which include the harness default) one whole lattice plane per axis flips sides. Default 5x5x5 cloud: 61 of 125 pixels (48.8%) differ, 75 individual channel flips, mean brightness orig 102 vs port 153 (+50%). The colour histograms are exact mirrors of each other — orig {black 27, R 18, G 18, Y 12, B 18, M 12, C 12, white 8}; port {black 8, R 12, G 12, Y 18, B 12, M 18, C 18, white 27}. The original's black octant is a 3x3x3 corner and its white octant a 2x2x2 corner; the port has those two swapped.

Same effect scales with lattice parity: 3^3 mean 85 vs 170 (orig black = 2x2x2, white = 1 pixel; port the reverse), 7^3 109 vs 146, 11^3 116 vs 139, 21^3 121 vs 134 — the gap shrinks as the midplane becomes a smaller fraction of the cloud, and vanishes on even sides.

On FLAT rigs the divergence is a whole-channel difference, because the harness pins z at exactly 0.5. --rig grid --grid 16x16: orig draws four quadrants {black, red, green, yellow} at 64 px each; port draws the same four quadrants with blue forced on everywhere — {blue, magenta, cyan, white} at 64 px each. The x/y quadrant split is identical on both sides (16 is even, so no x/y coordinate hits 0.5). --rig strip --pixels 60 shows the same thing: orig {black 16, red 16, green 16, yellow 12}, port the identical grouping with +blue on all 60 pixels. So on any 2D installation the port renders the original's picture with the blue channel railed on.

Waterfall images agree with the numbers: both are perfectly vertical stripes (zero slope = zero motion) in the same colour families, but the port's leftmost black band is much narrower and its right end is white-dominated where the original's is cyan/white mixed.

Control surfaces MATCH: meta.json reports controls: [] on both sides, and --probe-controls found '(no settable controls)' on orig and port alike. Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors: false on both).

Both sides are seed-independent and wall-clock-independent: --seed 7 and --wall-clock 1756043400 reproduce the baseline means exactly (orig 102 / port 153) with no change in the dumped frame. No compile or runtime errors on either side in any run.
feedback: Single-cause fix: the port's octant test includes the exact midplane in the high half. The original turns a channel ON only when the normalized coordinate is STRICTLY above 0.5 — a pixel sitting at coord == 0.5 must render that channel OFF. Change the port's per-axis comparison from >= 0.5 to > 0.5 (equivalently, make the tie go to the LOW octant). Nothing else about the pattern needs touching.

Regression check after the fix: on the default 5x5x5 cloud the port's mean brightness must drop from 153 to 102, the black octant must grow from 8 to 27 pixels and the white octant shrink from 27 to 8, and the colour histogram must read {black 27, red 18, green 18, yellow 12, blue 18, magenta 12, cyan 12, white 8}.

Second regression check, more sensitive: --rig grid --grid 16x16 must render {black, red, green, yellow} — NOT the all-blue-on variants {blue, magenta, cyan, white} the port currently produces. Flat rigs pin z at exactly 0.5, so they expose this bug as a full-channel error and are the cheapest way to see it.

Do NOT use an even-sided cloud (e.g. --pixels 1000 → 10x10x10) to validate the fix: the two sides are already byte-identical there because no pixel lands on the midplane. Use an odd side (5^3 default, or 21^3 for fine threshold bracketing) or a flat rig.

No other work is needed: axis→channel mapping, the 8-corner palette, full-scale 0/255 channel values, static (zero-motion) behaviour over 600 s, absence of controls, and seed/wall-clock independence all already match the original exactly.
